question.prompt: Half the people in a room left. One third of those remaining started to dance. There were then \(12\) people who were not dancing. What was the original number of people in the room?

solutions.explanation:
Work backward from the \(12\) people who were not dancing. One third of those remaining danced, so the nondancers made up two of three equal groups.

Those two groups contained \(12\) people, so each group contained \(12\div2=6\) people. All three groups together therefore contained
\[
3\times6=18\text{ people}.
\]
These \(18\) people were the half who stayed. Doubling gives the original number:
\[
2\times18=36.
\]
The room originally contained \(36\) people, choice C.
solutions.title: Work backward with equal groups
